objective: Retire pi-primitives as a parallel plugin/resource framework by migrating each policy to native Pi resources or explicit extension policy code, narrowing the existing extension path to a compatibility policy bundle, and deferring physical rename or scaffold removal until an approved breaking-change window.

in: Inventory and characterize concise-output, implementation-file-completion, model-artifacts, whimsical, trigger matching, injection order, enablement, isolation, diagnostics, and configuration behavior.
Classify each primitive as a native skill, prompt, extension hook, or explicit package policy and migrate it to the smallest native boundary.
Remove internal discovery, resource loading, generic trigger/plugin abstractions, and central plugin-style registration where native Pi facilities replace them.
Keep extensions/pi-primitives as a narrowed compatibility policy bundle during this release unless a separately approved major-version revision authorizes renaming.
Recognize existing configuration and the deprecated whimsical policy safely, with clear migration/deprecation diagnostics.
Coordinate /scaffold primitive behavior with initiative 06 without assuming removal authorization.
out: Physically renaming pi-primitives to pi-policies in a non-major release.
Removing /scaffold primitive or breaking existing filter/config paths without explicit release approval and an intentional authority revision.
Creating a new Gentic registry, resource type, discovery system, or enable/disable mechanism.
Changing unrelated package profiles or native Pi discovery semantics.

constraints: Implementation follows initiatives 01-06 so shared boundaries and scaffolding ownership are settled first.
Use native Pi extensions, skills, prompts, hooks, package discovery, and configuration rather than recreating them.
Preserve applicable injected policy text, trigger semantics, registration order, and safe defaults until each migration is explicitly qualified.
Keep the extension path stable; the optional pi-policies rename is a major-release decision outside this initiative.
If /scaffold primitive cannot yet be removed, retain it for one release as compatible generation or an explicitly approved deprecation-only command; do not silently change it.
Malformed, unknown, oversized, or legacy configuration must remain bounded and produce actionable diagnostics.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every current primitive has an explicit native-resource or extension-policy destination with characterized behavior and migration tests.

The internal generic plugin framework—parallel discovery, generic resource loading, trigger abstraction, isolation wrapper, and central plugin-style registry—is removed where native Pi owns those concerns.
The retained extensions/pi-primitives path is a narrow compatibility policy bundle, not a new resource system, and existing supported configuration degrades safely with migration diagnostics.
The physical pi-policies rename and unapproved /scaffold primitive removal remain deferred; public filter/config behavior changes only through explicit approved compatibility decisions.
Prompt injection content/order, trigger behavior, safe defaults, and relevant package-profile behavior remain qualified, with inventories/docs updated.
Focused and full repository qualification passes with independent review that no parallel plugin architecture remains.

assessment.reason: Retiring a resource framework affects prompt policy, triggers, configuration, package profiles, scaffolding, and user-visible injections; migration must avoid both behavior drift and recreating the abstraction elsewhere.
surfaces: catalog inventory and resource validation tests
unknowns: The release owner has not approved removal of /scaffold primitive.
The optional pi-primitives to pi-policies physical rename is deferred to a major release.
Each primitive's best native destination must be confirmed against current Pi APIs and repository conventions.

practices.reason: Each primitive has distinct triggers and injection behavior and should not be migrated through a one-size-fits-all replacement.
The goal is to remove the parallel abstraction, not rename or relocate it.
Legacy config, scaffolding, package paths, prompt behavior, and inventories require explicit negative tests and release-aware review.

obligations.text: Characterize every primitive's policy text, trigger positives/negatives, injection order, enablement, safe defaults, isolation, diagnostics, legacy configuration, and package-profile behavior before migration.

Verify each policy uses a native or explicit extension boundary, the generic internal framework is removed, no replacement registry/resource type is introduced, and configuration remains bounded with actionable diagnostics.

Run primitive/policy, prompt, package, scaffold compatibility, inventory, typecheck, resource, command, performance, and full repository gates, then obtain independent review of framework retirement and compatibility decisions.

work.title: Characterize and map every primitive to a native destination

testing.approach: Build a per-policy behavior matrix and focused positive, negative, order, enablement, malformed-config, and profile fixtures before migration.
testing.reason: The policies are small but behaviorally different; each needs an explicit destination and baseline.

work.title: Migrate policies and remove the internal primitive framework

testing.approach: Move each policy to native resources or explicit hooks, delete superseded generic machinery, and test that no parallel registry/discovery/loading layer remains.
testing.reason: A native migration succeeds only when the obsolete abstraction is actually removed.

work.title: Apply compatibility gates and qualify retirement

testing.approach: Preserve or explicitly gate scaffold/path compatibility, refresh docs/inventories, run all declared gates, and obtain independent source-bound review.
testing.reason: Retirement must be safe for current users and must not smuggle in unapproved breaking changes.

decisions.text: Defer the physical pi-primitives to pi-policies rename.
decisions.basis: Package filter paths are public compatibility surfaces and the consolidation plan recommends a major-release gate.

decisions.text: Do not assume /scaffold primitive may be removed.
decisions.basis: The breaking-change window is unresolved; initiative 06 preserves it and this initiative requires explicit approval before changing it.

decisions.text: Migrate policies individually rather than creating a replacement generic framework.
decisions.basis: The reviewed defect is the existence of a plugin system inside Pi's plugin/resource system.

risks.text: Prompt policy text or trigger ordering changes during migration.
risks.mitigation: Use per-policy golden injection and ordering tests.

risks.text: The old framework is recreated under a policy name.
risks.mitigation: Review for discovery, generic loaders, trigger registries, and parallel enablement abstractions and reject them.

risks.text: Existing config or package filters break.
risks.mitigation: Keep the path stable, parse legacy fields safely, and emit bounded migration diagnostics.
Treat initiative 06's preserved behavior as the baseline and require explicit release approval before removal/deprecation changes.
